title: Glass Fallen the Wrong Way
content: The largest display shards lie outward from the orchid pedestal rather than inward from the roofline, suggesting the shattered panes were disturbed after the orchid was already handled.
visualDescription: A crescent of long glass shards fans away from the empty pedestal across the tiled walkway, with smaller safety fragments still clinging to the upper frame.
inventoryDescription: Photograph of glass shards fanning outward from the orchid display.
narrativeMeaning: The scene was staged to look like a chaotic accident, but the break pattern does not match a simple fall from above.

title: Gray Mineral Footprint by the Service Door
content: A pale gray footprint at the glasshouse service door contains mineral grit unlike the black greenhouse soil. It matches powder used around the pump room charity hampers and chapel stores.
visualDescription: A partial boot print in damp condensation beside the service door, its sole packed with light gray grit rather than dark potting soil.
inventoryDescription: Photograph of a gray mineral footprint at the service door.
narrativeMeaning: Someone entered or left through the service way after passing through an area connected to the mineral springs or chapel stores.

title: Dry Ring on the Orchid Pedestal
content: The pedestal is wet with lamp-mist except for a dry circular ring where the orchid pot sat. The ring has sharply dried edges, meaning the pot was removed several minutes before the lamps failed.
visualDescription: An empty marble pedestal with beads of moisture everywhere except a clean dry circle at the center, its edge visibly crisp under returning lamplight.
inventoryDescription: Photograph of the dry pot ring on the wet orchid pedestal.
narrativeMeaning: The orchid theft was not a spontaneous act during the darkness; it began before the public blackout.

title: Green Tying Twine on the Vent Latch
content: A strand of green gardener's twine is caught on the vent latch, seeming to implicate Marta. The strand is brittle and sun-faded, likely from an old plant tie rather than tonight's work.
visualDescription: A faded green fiber snagged on a brass vent latch above the broken display area, dry and frayed at both ends.
inventoryDescription: Photograph of old green twine snagged on the vent latch.
narrativeMeaning: It points suspiciously toward the gardener at first, but its age makes it a misleading trace rather than proof.

title: Silas Fen's Debt Telegram
content: A telegram tucked beside a pump room saucer demands payment from Silas by dawn and mentions a foreign buyer seeking 'night stock of exceptional rarity.'
visualDescription: A folded telegram under a mineral-water saucer, with the words 'payment by dawn' and 'foreign buyer' visible through damp paper.
inventoryDescription: Photograph of Silas Fen's urgent debt telegram.
narrativeMeaning: Silas had a powerful motive to steal the orchid, but the document alone does not place him inside the glasshouse at the decisive time.

title: Voss Saw a Gray-Dusted Figure
content: Pressed on his pump room alibi, Dr. Voss admits he saw a gray-dusted figure pass from the corridor toward Bellweather just after midnight, but he kept silent to avoid being drawn into scandal.
visualDescription: No physical photograph; this clue is recorded as SirLocked's interview note after confronting Voss.
inventoryDescription: Interview note: Voss saw a gray-dusted figure heading toward the estate.
narrativeMeaning: The footprint trace corresponds to a witnessed movement, tightening the timeline around the service route.

title: Chapel Charity Hampers with Mineral Powder
content: The pump room charity hampers are dusted with pale mineral powder from spring-salt wrappings. Their labels show Reverend Pike was arranging delivery through the chapel vestry shortly before midnight.
visualDescription: Stacked wicker hampers marked for the chapel vestry, their handles and nearby floor dusted with the same pale gray powder seen in the glasshouse print.
inventoryDescription: Photograph of mineral-dusted chapel charity hampers.
narrativeMeaning: The gray powder is tied to Pike's movements, not to ordinary garden work.

title: Blotter Impression Naming Pike
content: The professor's desk blotter preserves a reversed impression: 'Pike trustee sales... Oath clause void if concealed.' Marrow had evidence connecting Pike to improper sales from the Bellweather collection.
visualDescription: A green leather blotter under angled light, showing faint reversed words pressed into the surface beside an empty rectangle where a journal had lain.
inventoryDescription: Photograph of the blotter impression naming Pike and the oath clause.
narrativeMeaning: This supplies a concealed motive: the professor was preparing to expose Pike's abuse of his trustee position.

title: Livia's Lawyer Appointment
content: A calendar entry and rain-spotted calling card show Livia had already arranged to meet a solicitor about refusing immediate sale of Bellweather, undermining the idea that she urgently killed for inheritance.
visualDescription: A desk calendar opened to the following morning with 'Harrow & Vale, estate restraint' written beside a solicitor's damp calling card.
narrativeMeaning: Livia had inheritance concerns, but her documented plan points to preserving the estate rather than profiting from murder.

title: Livia Reveals the Oath's Silence
content: After being confronted with the blotter, Livia admits the household swore not to discuss the old Glasshouse Oath: a trustee scandal could strip Bellweather's private collection and expose years of quiet sales.
visualDescription: No physical photograph; this clue is recorded as an interview note after confronting Livia with the blotter.
inventoryDescription: Interview note: Livia explains why the oath frightened the household.
narrativeMeaning: The oath was not sentimental family folklore; it was a legal and social threat to whoever had exploited the collection.

title: Chapel Wax and Cassock Fiber on the Service Hatch
content: The cellar-side service hatch bears fresh chapel taper wax and a black wool fiber consistent with Reverend Pike's cassock. The hatch gives direct access to the glasshouse service door and lamp control line.
visualDescription: A low iron hatch with a smear of amber candle wax on the latch plate and a short black wool fiber caught in a splinter near the pull chain.
inventoryDescription: Photograph of chapel wax and black fiber on the cellar service hatch.
narrativeMeaning: This is the strongest late physical link between Pike and the hidden route used to stage the blackout and move the orchid.

title: Hidden Crate with Orchid and Journal
content: Behind old propagation frames is a ventilated crate containing the missing orchid and Marrow's research journal. The crate is sealed with a chapel-office paper band bearing Pike's impression.
visualDescription: A slatted crate tucked behind dusty frames, with pale orchid petals visible through the vents and a broken paper band stamped with the chapel office seal.
inventoryDescription: Photograph of the hidden orchid crate and missing journal.
narrativeMeaning: The stolen object and the motive document were hidden together by someone with chapel materials and access.
